final_candidates.decision_summary: Proline at Ile10 disrupts backbone hydrogen bonding in the predicted N-terminal beta-strand, strongly destabilizing the fold.
V36P creates a P35-P36 double-proline motif in the predicted central strand, which is incompatible with beta-sheet geometry and should severely misfold PsaE.
Removes a bulky core aromatic (Phe40) while imposing proline conformational constraints, combining core-packing loss with strand disruption.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 mutations are mechanistically independent and mutually complementary; additional self-iteration would not improve them.

history.rationale: Introduces proline into a hydrophobic N-terminal region, likely breaking secondary structure and disrupting core packing in this small 68-aa protein.
Proline substitution in the N-terminal beta-rich region breaks backbone hydrogen bonding and is strongly destabilizing.
Proline at a buried hydrophobic leucine adjacent to I10 should strongly destabilize any helix/strand and impair folding.
Adjacent to I10P but overlapping effects; kept as backup but ranked below independent core disruptions.

Removes a bulky hydrophobic core aromatic and imposes proline constraints in a strand region, both destabilizing.
Proline replacement of a buried valine mid-sequence is expected to disrupt local structure and destabilize the small protein.
Creates a Pro35-Pro36 double-proline motif in the predicted central beta-strand, which should severely disrupt the sheet and fold; reranked up.
Removing the large tryptophan side chain to glycine eliminates core hydrophobic packing and adds conformational flexibility, likely destabilizing the fold.
